characters.name: Solid Snake
characters.identity: FOXHOUND rookie on Operation Intrude N313
characters.outer_goal: Find Gray Fox, investigate and destroy Metal Gear
characters.inner_conflict: Trust in his mentor and command versus the evidence he must act on himself
characters.beginning: Follows his CO and relies on authoritative instructions
characters.turn: Rescues Fox, confronts manipulated guidance, earns relationships beyond chain of command
characters.end: Defeats the Outer Heaven leader and escapes without uncritical reliance on command
characters.story_boundary: No knowledge of Big Boss's later-canon identity retcon while playing the 1995 mission

characters.name: Gray Fox / Grey Fox
characters.identity: FOXHOUND's senior Fox operative; earlier infiltration failed
characters.outer_goal: Pass actionable Metal Gear intelligence to Snake
characters.inner_conflict: Competent elite soldier rendered vulnerable by captivity, yet still an ally rather than a failed-objective token
characters.beginning: Missing operative whose fate drives the first investigation
characters.turn: Discovered in the adjacent prison cell after Snake is deliberately captured; reveals the nuclear threat and points to Madnar
characters.end: Survives rescue; his whereabouts after this encounter are not authoritatively expanded within the 1987 game
characters.story_boundary: Do not give Fox a 1995 cyborg body, a new 1995 betrayal, or a second mandatory confrontation; later games' events are future

characters.name: Big Boss / commanding officer
characters.identity: Snake's trusted FOXHOUND commander and hidden Outer Heaven antagonist
characters.outer_goal: Direct the field operation while concealing his role in Outer Heaven
characters.inner_conflict: The persona of the mentor becomes incompatible with mounting evidence of deliberate sabotage
characters.beginning: Helpful mission-giver with equipment and route advice
characters.turn: Suspicious guidance escalates to explicit operational obstruction
characters.end: Confronted as the enemy behind the fortress at the end of the original 1987 plot
characters.story_boundary: Later-canon Venom Snake distinction should be optional post-credits hindsight, not exposed to in-world Snake as 1995 truth

characters.name: Kyle Schneider
characters.identity: Former fortress architect and resistance leader
characters.outer_goal: Dismantle the fortress that destroyed his family
characters.inner_conflict: Knowledge of the structure versus danger to everyone involved in resistance
characters.beginning: Unknown radio source who knows the actual built environment
characters.turn: Gives practical route, equipment and wall information that changes traversal
characters.end: Transmission is interrupted as he approaches disclosure of the enemy leadership
characters.story_boundary: Do not depict his later MG2 identity as a 1995 character fact; fate of interrupted call is not definitively resolved here

characters.name: Diane
characters.identity: Resistance operative and former Thin Wall vocalist
characters.outer_goal: Protect the resistance and keep Snake alive around specialized threats
characters.inner_conflict: Operational commitment and the personal risk of caring about the infiltrator
characters.beginning: Knowledgeable contact, initially practical
characters.turn: Enemy-specific advice grows into a working alliance across bosses
characters.end: Personal farewell as Snake faces a threat beyond her knowledge
characters.story_boundary: Her exact emotional language and Steve relationship are version-specific; do not assert romance beyond original script

characters.name: Jennifer
characters.identity: Undercover medical-staff member seeking imprisoned brother
characters.outer_goal: Rescue her brother while sabotaging Outer Heaven from within
characters.inner_conflict: Maintaining cover while putting her personal stake ahead of self-preservation
characters.beginning: Resistance insider with unknown personal motive to Snake
characters.turn: Helps procure weaponry and bypass barriers; reveals her brother among hostages held by Coward Duck
characters.end: Brother's liberation makes her warning and escape help personally consequential
characters.story_boundary: Keep brother's identity unnamed until supported by the chosen script; don't give him invented rank or crimes

characters.name: Dr. Pettrovich / Drago Pettrovich Madnar
characters.identity: Engineer coerced into TX-55 development
characters.outer_goal: Secure Ellen's freedom before revealing how to destroy his creation
characters.inner_conflict: Technical responsibility versus the need to protect his daughter
characters.beginning: Rumoured source of Metal Gear's vulnerabilities
characters.turn: Rescued but refuses to disclose vital information until Ellen is saved
characters.end: After Ellen rescue, supplies the necessary destruction method and location
characters.story_boundary: Do not make him willingly proud of building TX-55 in this 1995 story or pull later MG2 choices into his 1987 rescue

characters.name: Ellen Pettrovich / Ellen Madnar
characters.identity: Madnar's daughter; former ballet performer, kidnapped hostage
characters.outer_goal: Regain freedom and help her father survive
characters.inner_conflict: Held as coercive leverage without being reduced to an inventory key
characters.beginning: Missing hostage whose captivity blocks Madnar's cooperation
characters.turn: Snake reaches and protects her; she conveys the coercion behind Metal Gear
characters.end: Rescued; objective to return information and secure father is acknowledged
characters.story_boundary: No invented armed-combat role or unilateral machine disarm; allow a human-scale agency beat without adding false canon

characters.name: Jennifer's brother
characters.identity: Prisoner used as a hostage by Coward Duck
characters.outer_goal: Survive and escape detention
characters.inner_conflict: Protect other prisoners and remain alive during firefight
characters.beginning: Identity withheld from Snake until Jennifer's radio disclosure
characters.turn: Player must avoid harming captives during Coward Duck encounter
characters.end: Liberated; provides escape-related information where source supports it
characters.story_boundary: No independent pre-1987 service record or personality asserted without evidence

characters.name: Shoot Gunner / Shotmaker
characters.identity: Source-named prison escape boss with a shotgun
characters.outer_goal: Stop any prisoner escape
characters.inner_conflict: Authority comes from controlling a confined fighting space; personal past is not given by the original game
characters.beginning: A feared unseen threat protecting the detention route
characters.turn: Challenges Snake immediately after the hard-won rescue and equipment recovery
characters.end: Defeat opens the escape trajectory; no invented familial or ideological confession
characters.story_boundary: Keep a readable shotgun commitment, role-grounded environment and source-authentic beat; detailed origin would be remake invention

characters.name: Machinegun Kid
characters.identity: Source-named machine-gun boss
characters.outer_goal: Hold a defended access route
characters.inner_conflict: His battlefield identity is a heavy suppression role; personal biography is source-limited
characters.beginning: Rumours or signs of a strongly held corridor
characters.turn: Player solves suppression through positioning, not pure health attrition
characters.end: The route opens after winning a meaningful confrontation
characters.story_boundary: No asserted age, childhood or psychological diagnosis just because the codename is 'Kid'

characters.name: Fire Trooper
characters.identity: Source-named flame-weapon boss
characters.outer_goal: Prevent access to a critical prisoner route
characters.inner_conflict: Risky area-denial behaviour should reveal tactical commitment rather than invented trauma
characters.beginning: Hazard signage and heat damage foreshadow a protected zone
characters.turn: Boss pressures cover, retreat routes and safe timing
characters.end: Source route is recovered; area hazards cease for believable physical reasons
characters.story_boundary: No secret character transformation or invented identity reveal

characters.name: Coward Duck / Dirty Duck
characters.identity: Source-named boomerang boss with human hostages
characters.outer_goal: Survive by using captives as protection
characters.inner_conflict: Self-preservation is expressed in a concrete morally pressured fight; original offers no detailed life history
characters.beginning: Jennifer's brother is believed captive, so Snake knows stakes ahead of encounter
characters.turn: Fighting around human shields makes target choice and positioning matter
characters.end: Safe hostages and Card 8 preserve source rewards and consequences
characters.story_boundary: Never treat hostages as disposable targets; preserve source character function and name variants

characters.name: Outer Heaven fortress commander / Big Boss's phantom (Venom Snake)
characters.identity: Physical final adversary presented to Snake as Big Boss; later MGSV continuity identifies him as Big Boss's double
characters.outer_goal: Defend Outer Heaven and its independence during the 1995 uprising
characters.inner_conflict: Carries the inherited legend and commands in its name; precise feelings during Snake's mission are not depicted by the 1987 game
characters.beginning: Unseen leader whose identity is withheld from Snake
characters.turn: The imprisoned witness reveals the Big Boss identity; Snake reaches the final commander amid TX-55's destruction
characters.end: Apparently defeated by Snake, fortress self-destructs; later canon treats the fallen commander as the phantom
characters.story_boundary: Preserve Snake's 1995 perception of confronting Big Boss. Never reveal the double or discuss his medic origin to Snake in this game; treat as postgame lore

characters.name: Steve
characters.identity: Diane's brother in later canon, who occasionally answers her radio in the Japanese original
characters.outer_goal: Support Diane while she helps Snake
characters.inner_conflict: Protectiveness and irritation when Snake repeatedly contacts his sister
characters.beginning: Occasional unexpected voice in Diane's frequency
characters.turn: Tells Snake she is unavailable at specific moments
characters.end: No source 1995 physical fate or personal climax
characters.story_boundary: Steve's lines were removed from original European MSX release; their presence in selected J2ME is unverified. Optional only

characters.name: TX-11 Arnold / Bloody Brad pair
characters.identity: Two experimental cyberoid enforcers built by Madnar
characters.outer_goal: Prevent Snake leaving the Building Two secured level
characters.inner_conflict: No human interior psychology: they embody Madnar's inventions being used as jailers
characters.beginning: Rumoured supposedly invincible protectors near research/prisoners
characters.turn: Resist ordinary gunfire and pressure heavy-weapon acquisition
characters.end: Destroying the pair yields Card 7 and exposes another route toward Ellen
characters.story_boundary: Never give androids childhood, self-awareness, or emotional motivations absent from 1987 script

characters.name: False Dr. Pettrovich contact
characters.identity: Outer Heaven's misleading captive/scientist trap before reaching the real Madnar
characters.outer_goal: Mislead Snake into an ambush
characters.inner_conflict: None established; representation is a deception tactic, not a named character biography
characters.beginning: Prisoner intel gives a plausible but false basement location
characters.turn: Ambush reveals scientist location claim was deliberately deceptive
characters.end: Snake survives and discovers actual holding location
characters.story_boundary: Do not infer decoy is a known historical figure or secretly Madnar himself

characters.name: Outer Heaven prisoners and resistance witnesses
characters.identity: Unnamed captives who give physical-route, rank, identity and threat intelligence
characters.outer_goal: Survive detention and pass on information after rescue
characters.inner_conflict: Fear that no one outside will believe or reach them; don't replace with a generic collectible
characters.beginning: Early prisoners show human stakes and furnish leads on Fox and local allies
characters.turn: Further prisoners direct Snake toward scientist, hidden walls, Jennifer and high-security passages
characters.end: Late basement witness identifies Big Boss; survivor status otherwise limited to rescue events
characters.story_boundary: Do not invent twenty-five unique biographies without source; POW rescues should be individually authored only once source identities confirmed

characters.name: Outer Heaven security and ordinary soldiers
characters.identity: Fortress patrol, maintenance, detention, vehicle and research security force
characters.outer_goal: Hold positions and prevent infiltration
characters.inner_conflict: Operational loyalty and doubt may be explored only as non-canonical ambient interpretation
characters.beginning: Guards emerge from trucks and make early patrol routine intelligible
characters.turn: Capture Snake; operate alarms, disinformation traps and escalating base response
characters.end: Losing the machine and command structure triggers evacuation or chaos; do not automatically shoot every retreating soldier
characters.story_boundary: Avoid invented named war crimes or widespread secret knowledge of Big Boss's dual identity

characters.name: Hind D helicopter crew
characters.identity: Unnamed aircraft crew controlling a major courtyard/roofspace encounter
characters.outer_goal: Keep air-access route secure
characters.inner_conflict: None canonically given; threat defined by aircraft and deployment duty
characters.beginning: Helicopter access is foreshadowed by flight deck, sound and sightlines
characters.turn: Snake survives the Hind D encounter with appropriate equipment/cover
characters.end: Aircraft disabled/destroyed as original progression allows
characters.story_boundary: No invented pilot name, family history or defection

characters.name: Tank and bulldozer crews
characters.identity: Unnamed vehicle operators serving as traversability and survival encounters
characters.outer_goal: Control exterior crossings and restrict movement
characters.inner_conflict: None specified; dramatize logistics of the fortress rather than personal biography
characters.beginning: Vehicles, repair bays and roadways make threat plausible
characters.turn: Tank and bulldozer encounters challenge preparation/spacing
characters.end: Player overcomes vehicle obstacles and reaches next compound
characters.story_boundary: Do not assign personal biographies; credible vehicles are not personal villains

characters.name: TX-55 Metal Gear
characters.identity: Nuclear-capable bipedal weapons system, not a sentient character
characters.outer_goal: An instrument of Outer Heaven's strategic ambitions
characters.inner_conflict: No subjective mind; story purpose is the tangible object of Snake's mission and Madnar's coercion
characters.beginning: A mysterious name in Gray Fox's last transmission
characters.turn: Fox explains its nuclear capability; Madnar identifies the destruction sequence
characters.end: Snake plants the required explosives on the machine's feet, destroys it and begins final collapse
characters.story_boundary: Do not turn original MG1 TX-55 into REX, a voiced boss, or a fight to shoot an autonomous AI pilot

policy: Never substitute character biography for playable interaction
Never add mandatory Gray Fox second appearance in 1995 without canonical verification
In-world characters do not know later-series reveals
A boss may have personality and environmental history without a fabricated canonical origin
Tie each critical reveal to a stable event flag, physical location, persistent transcript, and interrupted-play path
Keep older rescue and radio prototypes but mark unimplemented rest of full-game arcs
All beats must be reconciled against J2ME before being promoted to original-source verified
Named bosses have distinct source-limited character contracts; do not invent canonical psychology or family history.
Ellen location is Building One basement hidden wall; do not place her in Building Three.
Metal Gear destruction precedes commander's final confrontation and triggers self destruct pressure.
Treat 1987 source censorship/localization variants (Steve, radio lines) explicitly; compare J2ME before importing.
dependency_semantics: Narrative ordering/context only; never automatically wire depends_on as hard mission gates. Source-required radio/POW mechanics such as Jennifer's rank-gated rocket launcher and physical door are separately modelled as progress prerequisites.

gate_policy.critical: Only specific source-comparative gameplay requirements, then J2ME-verified version, may block progression
gate_policy.optional_radio: Optional exposition/advice radio never gates physical progression; Jennifer's source-required equipment/door calls are explicit exceptions, with accessible POW/rank recovery
gate_policy.hindsight: Later-era character identity not disclosed to in-world Snake in 1995
gate_policy.location: Anchors provisional until verified against the chosen J2ME 3.3.0 data
